question: The position vectors of three points are $\overrightarrow{OA}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{OC}=7\hat{i}-7\hat{j}+17\hat{k}$.(a) Obtain $\overrightarrow{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{BC}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$.(b) Show that the three points are collinear.(c) Verify the result by comparing the distances $AB$, $BC$ and $AC$.
explanation: (a)`\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{OB}-\overrightarrow{OA}\overrightarrow{AB}=(3-1)\hat{i}+(-1-2)\hat{j}+[5-(-1)]\hat{k}\overrightarrow{AB}=2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+6\hat{k}`Similarly,`\overrightarrow{BC}=\overrightarrow{OC}-\overrightarrow{OB}\overrightarrow{BC}=4\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+12\hat{k}`Also,`\overrightarrow{AC}=\overrightarrow{OC}-\overrightarrow{OA}\overrightarrow{AC}=6\hat{i}-9\hat{j}+18\hat{k}`(b)From the obtained vectors,`\overrightarrow{BC}=2\overrightarrow{AB}`and`\overrightarrow{AC}=3\overrightarrow{AB}`Therefore, $\overrightarrow{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{BC}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ are parallel and have the same direction. Hence, the points $A$, $B$ and $C$ are collinear.(c)`AB=\sqrt{2^2+(-3)^2+6^2}=7BC=\sqrt{4^2+(-6)^2+12^2}=14AC=\sqrt{6^2+(-9)^2+18^2}=21`Thus,`AB+BC=7+14=21=AC`Final ResultSince $AB+BC=AC$, the point $B$ lies between $A$ and $C$. Therefore, $A$, $B$ and $C$ are collinear.

options.A:
(a) $\overrightarrow{AB}=2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+6\hat{k}$, $\overrightarrow{BC}=4\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+12\hat{k}$, $\overrightarrow{AC}=6\hat{i}-9\hat{j}+18\hat{k}$
(b) $\overrightarrow{BC}=2\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}=3\overrightarrow{AB}$, so the points are collinear.
(c) $AB=7$, $BC=14$, $AC=21$ and $AB+BC=AC$.
